mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average compresses discount rates for equity valuations, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 0.50% in a 3-month window, it signals an imminent monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.50% over 3 months, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in the unemployment rate above 0.2 percentage points in 3 months signals a strong economy with tightening monetary policy, which reduces equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls by >0.2pp in 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in housing starts below 1500 thousand units and a drop in retail sales below 620 billion dollars signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances during late-cycle expansion when HOUST < 1500 and RSAFS < 620, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5.0% relative to its 12-month moving average indicates a tightening labor market that boosts corporate earnings growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE is below 5.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production falls below 98.0 in a 3-month window, it signals a weakening manufacturing sector that reduces corporate profits, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO is below 98.0 over 3 months, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in GDP growth and housing starts below 1550 thousand units signals a weakening economic momentum, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 declines and HOUST < 1550 in 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-recovery regime, a sustained increase in employment growth above 100 thousand persons per month signals a strong labor market that supports consumer spending, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances during post-recovery when PAYEMS growth exceeds 100k, or the Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.
